## Overview

`@tuturuuu/human-check` is a platform-owned jigsaw puzzle for surfaces where
Cloudflare Turnstile cannot run: a content blocker, Safari Lockdown Mode or
iCloud Private Relay blocking `challenges.cloudflare.com`, or a browser Turnstile
reports as unsupported. It loads no third-party script. Turnstile stays the
primary check; the puzzle is offered only after Turnstile stalls.

The package has two entry points:

- `@tuturuuu/human-check`: a framework-free core (WebCrypto only) that renders
  challenges, verifies placements and issues and redeems pass tokens. It runs in
  Workers, Node and browsers.
- `@tuturuuu/human-check/react`: `JigsawCheck`, the drag and keyboard component.
  Callers inject `load`, `verify`, `onPass` and localized labels.

Meet guest join is the first consumer. Other surfaces (for example calendar
invitations) can reuse it by adding their own scope and routes.

## Security model

- **Server-authoritative answer.** The server renders a 320×160 raster PNG
  background (gradient, blobs, per-pixel noise) with the slot and two decoy
  cutouts of the same shape and darkness, plus the piece cut from the untouched
  background. Geometry comes from its own CSPRNG draw, separate from the
  texture, so the visible noise never reveals the slot. The slot position is
  sealed with AES-GCM under a key derived from `HUMAN_CHECK_SECRET`; the browser
  receives only the images, the piece row, the size and an opaque token. The
  images are raster, never SVG, so the markup cannot reveal the geometry.
- **Binding.** A challenge is bound to a scope (Meet uses `meet:<meetingId>`) and
  to an HMAC of the requesting network, and expires after two minutes.
- **Verification.** The placement must land within 6 px of the slot (4 px at the
  harder level). The pointer trajectory must look like a person dragging: enough
  samples, a plausible duration and peak speed, no teleport jumps, and not a
  constant-velocity flat line. Keyboard placement (arrow keys, Shift for larger
  steps, Enter) is the accessible path and needs deliberate steps over time.
- **Attempts and single use.** Each challenge allows three placements (two at
  the harder level) and issues at most one pass. The pass is an HMAC-signed token bound to the same scope and
  network, valid for two minutes, and redeemable once.
- **Counters.** Attempt, single-use and pass counters use the shared abuse-guard
  Durable Object when the app runs with it. Without it they count per isolate,
  and the two-minute lifetimes bound any replay.

The motion screen raises the cost of naive automation; it is not a bot detector
on its own. Every issue, pass and failure is rate-limited and scored, and Meet
still requires host approval for every guest.

## Limits in Meet

- Puzzles are charged before any database lookup: six per network per meeting
  every ten minutes, and sixty per meeting across networks. After half the
  network budget the puzzle adds a decoy and tightens tolerance; past the budget
  the network cools down until the window resets (`429` with `Retry-After`).
- Placements are charged first against a per-network budget across all
  puzzles and meetings: six every ten minutes. This bounds blind guessing (each
  placement covers about 7% of slot positions) and the verify route's work.
  Issuance also has a per-network window across all meetings (twenty every ten
  minutes).
- Issuance is scored with the
  [adaptive abuse policy](/build/devops/adaptive-abuse-rate-limits); restricted
  or challenge-required subjects get no puzzle. Passes and failures are recorded
  as `challenge_passed` and `challenge_failed` signals. Forged, expired and spent
  tokens are refused without a reputation write.
- A redeemed pass gives the same verified guest session as Turnstile, so the
  guest can vote in polls. The guest still waits in the lobby for the host.

## Accepted limits

- A computer-vision solver can place the piece; the motion screen is friction.
  Host approval, the rate limits and abuse scoring remain the real gate.
- Without the shared Durable Object, counters live per isolate. An attacker who
  floods one isolate can evict single-use entries, and spreading requests across
  isolates multiplies the placement budget; the two-minute token lifetimes bound
  the replay.
- Network binding and per-network limits use the client IP from Cloudflare's
  headers. Meet is reachable only through Cloudflare custom domains, which
  set them; a direct origin would let a client choose its network value.

## Configuration

Set `HUMAN_CHECK_SECRET` (at least 32 characters, from a CSPRNG) as a Worker
secret on `tuturuuu-meet`, for example with `wrangler secret put` from a
credentialed machine, reading the value from standard input. Without it the
puzzle routes answer `503` and the join page keeps **Retry verification** and
**Ask the host to let you in**. Rotating the secret invalidates outstanding
challenges and passes, which expire within two minutes anyway.

Regression coverage: `packages/human-check/src/challenge.test.ts`,
`motion.test.ts`, `react/jigsaw-check.test.tsx`, Meet's
`guest-human-check.test.ts`, the `human-check` route tests, the guest join
`route.test.ts` and `guest-join.test.tsx`.
